title: When can a small change be a standalone Task?
question: When can a small change be a standalone Task?
answer:
E-9: At workbench/tasks/TK-XXXX/TASK.md beside the Specs, under the same ADR-000I folder lifecycle, in the same Workbench-unique TK- series. Its card has an empty spec field and moves through lanes on its own. Used for small localized changes; a standalone Task that outgrows one context unit becomes a Spec.
TT-Q3: A Workbench is a 'room' that holds many Workbenches and many Projects; each Project has exactly one Workbench of its own. A Workbench is one set of Contract and routing artifacts with one Blueprint. A Blueprint has many Specs and many Tasks; a Spec has many Tasks and many Chats; a Task maps to one Chat. Spec is the destination, Task the steps; small work may be a standalone Task.
FND-Q17c: Specs nest and block each other, the same way Tasks do: "SPECs can nest and block each other, same as tasks. we are changing that." In the same message he said a Task can be created and merged into integration without a Spec branch.
SCR-7A: The full hierarchy still runs: Dispatcher -> Worker -> Dispatcher -> Director, with Git integration -> Task branch -> integration -> integration. The Dispatcher sends the Worker from integration, verifies and merges the result, and the Director checks it on integration. No role works from main. A direct Task that outgrows one context or repeats one objective becomes a Spec.
